why_this_corpus: frozen polyglot fixture tree: committed, offline, and its digest moves only on a deliberate fixture change, so a baseline stays comparable across releases. crates/codingest/src is the code under test and its digest moves nearly every release, which would make the gate REFUSE every time.
stored_value: min of 3 runs per query (repeatable inner loop); build_secs is the mean of 3 runs (once-per-build cost has no floor to find)
build_gating: recorded, not enforced: at 46 KB the build is dominated by one-time grammar init. Node/edge counts carry the build-side signal and are deterministic here (zero spread across three runs in both modes).
stability_across_3_runs: worst per-query median spread was 0.001 ms docs-on (eq_filter_pub) and 0.002 ms docs-off (defs_per_file), across three post-warmup runs per mode -- one to two 1 microsecond quantization ticks. Node and edge counts were identical in all runs (567/880 docs-on, 560/859 docs-off) and every cross-build parity flag held. build_secs means were 0.015 s docs-on from per-run 0.015/0.0145/0.0155 and 0.013 s docs-off from 0.013/0.013/0.013. FLOORS HELD AT 0.0075 IN BOTH MODES, as 0.2.20 through 0.2.22 did: 2.5x a one- or two-tick spread sits at or below the instrument's own resolution-derived jitter, and a too-tight floor blocks a future tag asymmetrically against a too-loose one that still trips on the 2x this backstop exists to catch. varlen_callers_1_3 remains the control: stored at 0.029 ms docs-on / 0.029 ms docs-off, 3.87x / 3.87x the floor, well over the 2x minimum, and flat versus the 0.2.22 record (0.029/0.030) across the kglite 0.17.6 -> 0.17.7 engine move and the methodology release -- neither touches an engine query path or a builder stage; the only builder-crate change is a new module no build path calls.
